question.leadin: During this war, UN forces were set back to a 140-mile defense line known as the "Pusan Perimeter" due to multiple defeats by the KPA.
question.text: Name this 1950s war that never ended with a peace treaty, but instead with the establishment of the DMZ. The U.S. and Soviet Union divided the namesake country of this war along the 38th parallel.
question.clue: Matthew Ridgeway replaced a general in this war who had turned the tide by landing an army behind enemy lines at Incheon.

swap.leadin: Give the following about medieval Asian warfare.
swap.text: In the 16th century, Yi Sun-sin perfected the design of the turtle ships used by the Joseon dynasty to defend this Asian peninsula from the invading Japanese navy. One modern country on this peninsula has capital Seoul.
swap.clue: This territory was the site of a war that was ended by a truce at Panmunjom.

question.leadin: Answer the following about pyramids around the world.
question.text: The pyramidal Ryugyong Hotel in this country remains unfinished despite its construction starting in 1987. A grand opening was planned in 2012 on the centenary of this country's "Eternal President" Kim Il-Sung, but it was eventually scrapped.
question.answerHtml: North Korea [or Democratic People’s Republic of Korea; prompt on Korea]
question.clue: This country's first leader proposed the "Juche" ideology.

swap.leadin: Name these places identified with the Korean War.
swap.text: The UN army eventually almost took the whole Korean Peninsula before being repelled as it was approaching this river that separates North Korea from China.
swap.clue: The Friendship Bridge is the only remaining bridge over this river and connects the cities of Dandong and Sinujiu.

question.leadin: The yangban served as this dynasty's bureaucracy after passing the gwageo exam.
question.text: Sejong the Great was a member of what Korean dynasty which was opposed by the Donghak Uprising?
question.clue: This final dynastic kingdom of Korea that lasted from 1392 to 1897 when it was replaced by the Korean Empire. Sejong the Great established the Hall of Worthies in this kingdom.

swap.text: Yi utilized ships named for these animals, which some say is an early type of ironclad. Those ships had armor that was said to resemble these animals' shells.
swap.clue: Soldiers from Ming China helped defend Korea from Japanese invasion at the end of the 16th century. During that conflict, Korean Admiral Yi utilized these crazy awesome vessels which received their name from the appearance caused by their armored decks.

question.leadin: Answer the following about numerically-named periods of Chinese history.
question.text: Cao Cao, Sun Quan, and Liu Bei fought for control of China during this era between the Han and Jin Dynasties. It is the namesake of a novel by Luo Guanzhong.
question.clue: The "Later" part of a period with this name was dominated by a Unified Silla that conquered Goguryeo.

swap.leadin: This kingdom ultimately broke up into the a group known as the Three Kingdoms, which included Baekje and Goguryeo.
swap.text: This kingdom was ruled by the Gyeongju Kim clan for nearly 1000 years, making it one of the longest-surviving dynasties in history. Its aristocrats were called "sacred bone" or "true bone".
swap.clue: Confucianism in Korea built upon earlier hierarchies such as the bone-rank system, which was used by this kingdom. This kingdom unified Korea in the 7th century after defeating its rivals Baekje and Goguryeo.

question.leadin: In reaction to his chief foreign rival winning an Olympics bid, this man ordered a bombing of Flight 858.
question.text: Identify this politician whose government developed the philosophy of "self-reliance" or juche.
question.clue: He agreed to the release of the crew of the Pueblo at Pammujan in 1968.

swap.leadin: Name these places important in the Korean War.
swap.text: Following the North's seizure of Seoul, this city became the temporary capital of the Republic of Korea. Its namesake "perimeter" was attacked by General Kim Chaek.
swap.clue: The Eighth Army set about defending a "perimeter" named for this South Korean Port city.

question.leadin: Name these Asian politicians who had European wives.
question.text: This first president of South Korea assumed dictatorial powers when the Korean War broke out, and was exiled with his Austrian wife Franziska Donner to Hawaii after his overthrow in a 1960 coup.
question.clue: Protests against him began after a fisherman discovered the dead body of a high schooler with a tear gas capsule lodged in his eye near the port city of Masan.

swap.leadin: Kings from this dynasty carried out purges of a faction of scholars known as the Sarim.
swap.text: Name this dynasty, an earlier king of which brought many scholars to his court in the Hall of Worthies. This dynasty fell into decline after its near-defeat in the Imjin War.
swap.clue: Members of the yangban (yong-bon) class were killed by followers of the "Eastern Learning" Donghak religion during this dynasty.

question.text: The Korean peninsula was introduced to Buddhism from China in the fourth century CE by Sundo, who mainly proselytized in this kingdom. Baekje, Silla, and this kingdom comprised the Korean Samhan.
question.clue: Some of the best-preserved art of this kingdom survives in the tomb of Dong Shou at a complex at Anak.

swap.leadin: This naval commander destroyed approximately 100 enemy ships at the Battle of Hansan Island without losing a single ship of his own.
swap.text: Name this admiral who leveraged the regular reversal of the tide to win the Battle of Myeongnyang ("myung-nyahng"). This undefeated Korean admiral used turtle ships to defend Korea during the Imjin War.

question.text: Passing the Gwageo was a requirement in Korea to become a member of this class of civil servants and aristocrats. Members of this class were also known as "mandarins."
question.clue: This class which constituted the aristocracy of a kingdom which was the last to select its officialdom through the gwageo examination system.

swap.text: The successful repulse of Japan extended the rule of this dynasty, under which the Hangul alphabet was created. It ruled until Japan finally conquered the peninsula in 1910.
swap.clue: Once led by Sejong the Great, this dynasty promulgated the hanggul script and pursued an isolationist policy that led it to be known as the "hermit kingdom."

question.leadin: It is the site of the Freedom Bridge over the Ijmin and the Bridge of No Return.
question.text: Name this "truce village" near Kaesong which was the site of peace talks which ended the Korean War.
question.clue: Both the Korean War and the Pueblo incident were ended by negotiations in this central Korean village on the Kyongui road.

swap.text: Chaebols have historically obtained preferential loans from the South Korean government through bribery, such as the 45 billion dollars given to Park Geun-hye by this de facto leader of Samsung, who served less than one year of a five-year prison sentence.

question.text: Prior to being mostly reversed by Lee Myung-bak, Kim Dae-jung's Sunshine Policy helped repair South Korea's relations with the regime of this co-producer of the assuredly tasteful film Diary of a Girl Student, a North Korean dictator with crazy hair and crazier everything else.
question.clue: His "Sunshine policy" tried to bolster the software industry, and he once abducted a movie director to shoot a socialist Godzilla flick.

swap.leadin: This kingdom was ruled by the Gyeongju Kim clan for most of its existence.
swap.text: Name this kingdom that united the clans of the Jinhan. It used the bone rank system.
swap.clue: This dynasty employed a cultured class of cosmetic-using soldiers called the "flowering knights," or "hwarang."
